clue.text: Relaxed eating soldier's medicinal plant

indicators.note: something eating takes another thing inside itself, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: comfy means relaxed and at ease
RE is the Royal Engineers, standard crossword shorthand for soldiers

explanation.surface: A laid-back soldier tucks into a herbal remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: COMFREY: the Royal Engineers sit inside COMFY, between the F and the Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Comfrey is a hairy herb long used in folk medicine to heal bruises and broken bones.

clue.text: Beetle keeps maiden on edge

indicators.note: something that keeps another holds it inside itself

parts.note: a chafer is a large beetle, such as the cockchafer
M is the cricket scorer's mark for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A beetle holds a young woman in suspense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On edge' reads as nervous; 'on' only joins, and 'edge' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamfer is a bevelled edge, a corner cut off at an angle on wood or stone.

clue.text: Medium Ishtar bewitched killed a bull

definitions.note: describes the god by his deed: he who killed a bull

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for medium

indicators.note: a bewitched thing is transformed by a spell, so the name's letters change places

parts.note: the Babylonian goddess's name, used as letters

explanation.surface: A spiritualist medium under a spell from a goddess slays a bull.
explanation.walkthrough: Ishtar is a goddess, fitting the mythic picture, but supplies only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Mithras, the Persian and Roman god, is always shown in temple carvings slaying a sacred bull.

clue.text: Racehorse going uphill is run over

indicators.note: in a down entry, going uphill means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a pacer is a harness-racing horse

explanation.surface: A racehorse climbing a slope gets hit by a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run over' suggests an accident; it means go through again briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise, quickly going back through the main points again.

clue.text: Drinker's challenge is ordeal Fay bungled

indicators.note: something bungled is botched, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: Fay botched a drinking contest and found it an ordeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Downing a yard-long glass of beer in one go is a traditional pub feat to test a toper.

clue.text: Supplement for Dutch chemical company during depression

indicators.note: what happens during something sits within its span, so these letters go inside the next word

parts.note: a col is a dip or pass between mountain peaks
D is the abbreviation for Dutch
Imperial Chemical Industries, the old British chemical giant

explanation.surface: Something about an add-on product from a Dutch chemical firm in hard times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' reads as economic slump, but it is a geographical dip in a ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A codicil is an addition appended to a will, amending or extending its terms.

clue.text: After tea, a couple of fellows banter

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
F is fellow, so two of them

explanation.surface: Two chaps chat lightly over tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaff is good-humoured teasing or light-hearted joking talk.

clue.text: Doctor hid Grace's execution

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters following are falsified into a new order

parts.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A doctor concealed the hanging of a woman called Grace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Execution' suggests a hanging; it means carrying out a duty.
explanation.definitionFit: The discharge of duties is their performance or carrying out, which is what execution means.

clue.text: Composer's heart's bad when climbing

parts.note: the core is the heart; the 's is 'is', joining

indicators.note: climbing in a down entry means the word runs from bottom to top

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: A composer's heart is failing on his climb up a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcangelo Corelli was an Italian Baroque violinist who wrote concerti grossi.

clue.text: General hides a cigarette in the greenery

indicators.note: one who hides something keeps it out of sight inside

parts.note: Robert E. Lee, the Confederate general
fag is British slang for a cigarette

explanation.surface: A general sneaks a smoke out in the bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: Leafage is foliage, the mass of leaves on plants making up greenery.

clue.text: A posh actor crashed vehicle

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a crashed thing is smashed up, so the word before it is broken and reassembled

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U speech
taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A well-to-do actor has had a car accident.
explanation.definitionFit: An autocar is an old term for a motor car, a self-propelled road vehicle.

clue.text: A student leaves one country for another

definitions.note: another country, set against the first

indicators.note: whatever leaves goes away, so those letters are dropped from the country

parts.note: the first country, which loses letters
taken as written
L is the learner plate on a car

explanation.surface: A student emigrates, swapping one nation for another.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the AL out of AUSTRALIA and AUSTRIA remains; 'another' points to the new country.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria is a separate nation in central Europe, a different country from the one the wordplay starts with.

clue.text: Refractory when turning to criticism

indicators.note: turning round means the little word is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: if can mean when, as in 'if it rains'
a reproof is a rebuke or criticism

explanation.surface: Someone stubborn when turning to face criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refractory' looks like obstinate, matching the criticism, but here it is the technical sense of heat-resisting.
explanation.definitionFit: Refractory materials withstand very high temperatures without burning or melting, as fireproof ones do.

clue.text: Sweet prince meets Virginia

parts.note: Prince Hal, the young Henry V in Shakespeare
VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state

explanation.surface: A charming prince is introduced to a woman called Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like an adjective for the prince, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Halva is a dense confection of sesame paste and sugar from the Middle East.

clue.text: Sticky stuff initially stuck in hold

indicators.note: in places that single letter inside the following word

parts.note: to rein is to hold back or restrain

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter only of the word it follows

parts.note: the opening letter of stuck

explanation.surface: Something gummy got stuck in a ship's hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold' suggests a ship's cargo space; it is the verb to restrain.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is the viscous, gummy secretion of trees such as pines, a classic sticky substance.

clue.text: Owen''s heel is mangled in the front of the plane

definitions.note: the clue names the place, the front of the aircraft, standing for the wheel found there; fair as 'in' marks it as something located at the nose

indicators.note: mangled things are crushed out of shape, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: Owen injures his heel at the front of an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram gives NOSEWHEEL; the key's NOSSWHEEL is a misprint.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosewheel is the landing wheel mounted under the forward fuselage of an aircraft.

clue.text: Vegetable popular in tavern

indicators.note: in tells us one word sits inside the other

parts.note: an auberge is a French inn
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A vegetable dish that goes down well in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The aubergine, called eggplant in America, is a purple-skinned fruit cooked as a vegetable.

clue.text: Crooner makes delivery on a beast

parts.note: in cricket a delivery is a ball bowled
taken as written
a deer is an animal

explanation.surface: A singer performs while riding an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' is a cricket term: each ball a bowler sends down is a delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: A balladeer is a singer of sentimental songs, much as a crooner is.

clue.text: Sea creature hit police sergeant? He will!

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or strike
PS is the abbreviation for police sergeant
the contraction of he will, written without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone dares to strike a police sergeant, and is told he certainly will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit' tempts you towards LAMP, but the police sergeant must keep both letters, so the verb is the old word for thrash. The question mark flags the forced split.
explanation.definitionFit: A lampshell is a brachiopod, a marine invertebrate with two hinged shells resembling an ancient oil lamp.

clue.text: Food in sink in the alley

indicators.note: in the places the first word inside the second

parts.note: a lane is a narrow alley
to sag is to sink or droop

explanation.surface: Food left in a kitchen sink out in the back alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sink' reads as the kitchen basin; it is the verb to droop.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is an Italian baked dish of flat pasta sheets layered with sauce.

clue.text: Game fellows tour the Republic of Botswana

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go round it, so one word encircles the other

parts.note: males are men or fellows
RB is Botswana's international vehicle code

explanation.surface: Sporting men go on tour to Botswana.
explanation.definitionFit: Marbles is a children's game of flicking small glass balls at one another.

clue.text: Decoration held by journalist in Bury

indicators.note: something held by another is clasped within it, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: ED is short for editor
Member of the Order of the British Empire, an honour

explanation.surface: A journalist from the Lancashire town of Bury receives an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury reads as the town near Manchester; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To embed something is to fix it firmly into a surrounding mass, which is burying it.

clue.text: British weapon page left in city

indicators.note: the page leaves the weapon and another letter takes its place

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
a pistol is a handgun

explanation.surface: A British gun left behind by a page in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing P from PISTOL leaves ISTOL, but nothing printed supplies the R that replaces it; the setter seems to mean 'page right', P becoming R.
explanation.definitionFit: Bristol is a major port city in south-west England.

clue.text: Long for shed of a particular manufacture

parts.note: to be dying for something is to long for it
to cast is to shed, as a snake casts its skin

explanation.surface: Pining for a garden hut of a special make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' reads as the garden building; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Die-cast objects are made by forcing molten metal into a mould, one specific production method.

clue.text: Son boasted of wages commonly

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
crew is an old past tense of crow, to brag

explanation.surface: A son brags about his pay packet.
explanation.definitionFit: Screw is old British slang for a salary or a person's weekly pay.

clue.text: Water is a barrier to pig

parts.note: taken as written
a dam is a barrier holding back a river
swine is another word for pigs

explanation.surface: Water bars the way for a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of SWINE completes the possessive in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's wine, or Adam's ale, is a jocular name for plain water, the only drink of the first man.

clue.text: Continue to play in London

definitions.note: a phrase of place rather than a noun, fair because the answer is defined as somewhere found within the capital

parts.note: to act is to play a part
on means continuing, as in go on

explanation.surface: An actor keeps performing in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase, 'act on' is to continue playing; Acton is an area of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Acton is a district of west London, in the borough of Ealing, so a place found in the city.

clue.text: Small bird's tail

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a tern is a seabird; the 's is 'is', joining

explanation.surface: The tail feathers of a little bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird's tail' wants to be one phrase; 'tail' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The stern is the rear of a ship, so its back end or tail.

clue.text: Great composer accepts student librettist

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for great

indicators.note: one who accepts something takes it in, so the following letter goes inside

parts.note: Jacques Ibert, the French composer
L for learner

explanation.surface: A celebrated composer takes on a pupil who writes his words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great composer' looks like one phrase; it splits into G plus Ibert.
explanation.definitionFit: W. S. Gilbert wrote the words for the Savoy operas set by Arthur Sullivan.

clue.text: Vengeful daughter to choose gunman

parts.note: to elect is to choose
RA is the Royal Artillery, whose men are gunners

explanation.surface: A daughter bent on revenge picks a hired gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gunman' suggests a killer, fitting the revenge plot; it is an artilleryman.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek tragedy Electra, child of Agamemnon, helps her brother kill their mother to avenge their father.

clue.text: Greek character gets over speech defect in time

indicators.note: in places that turned word inside the word for an age

parts.note: an eon is a vast period of time

indicators.note: turned over means the defect is written from back to front

parts.note: a lisp mispronounces s sounds

explanation.surface: A Greek man overcomes his stammer in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' sounds like a person; it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth letter of the Greek alphabet, the short e.

clue.text: Fibres coiled right around the fireplace

indicators.note: around means the abbreviation wraps about the word that follows

parts.note: RT is a standard abbreviation for right
an ingle is a hearth, as in inglenook

explanation.surface: Twisted threads lie round the hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a long spiral curl of hair, strands wound into a coil.
